title: A seal is non-empty for the whole run by design, and the contract never said so
body:
# 0027: A seal is non-empty for the whole run by design, and the contract never said so

## Tags

docs, seal, runlog

## Summary

`open_run_log` seeds a fresh `.errors` with the in-flight marker before the tool starts, so `[ -s .errors ]` is TRUE for the entire duration of a run. The reading-order contract carried this on the single word "completed" and never stated it, so a reader who checks a seal mid-run sees 84 bytes and concludes the gate failed.

## Reproduction

Reported by prolix/vc, who misread the marker as a failure three times in one day -- the third time after having already worked out what it was. That detail is the finding: knowing the mechanism did not stop the misreading, because the artifact looks exactly like a red seal.

## Root Cause

Documentation. The behaviour is correct and deliberate -- an aborted run must not read as green, which is what the marker is for. What was missing is the statement that a non-empty seal mid-run is NORMAL, and the pointer to `seal_is_inflight` as the way to tell the two apart.

`intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md` said `.errors` is "empty exactly when a *completed* run was green". True, and the entire distinction rested on one adjective that a reader looking at a live gate has no reason to weigh.

## Impact

No wrong behaviour. A competent operator loses time and, worse, may act on a verdict that has not been reached -- the failure mode is reading a run in progress as a run that failed.

## Proposed Fix

State it in the reading-order contract and in `usage-rules.md`, and name `seal_is_inflight` as the discriminator.

## Related

- 0019 -- the reading order this amends
- 0016 -- the in-flight sentinel's own history
- 0015 -- the run that sealed in-flight having completed, which is the opposite direction

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc).** A fourth bullet in the reading-order section of `ARCHITECTURE-shell.md` states that a non-empty `.errors` during a run is normal and means nothing has failed, names `seal_is_inflight` as the discriminator, and records that the word "completed" was carrying the distinction alone and did not survive contact. A matching NEVER in `usage-rules.md`.

Closed on the documentation, with no code change: the marker's behaviour is correct and this issue is about what was never written down. Prose is the deliverable, so there is no test -- the honest note being that this is the one of the three findings a gate cannot hold.
